_doc: PLACEHOLDER — the cluster's CONDUCTION data: per-era light rigs (the cold-light-winning arc), the ceiling witness geometry, the witness record plane's E1 anchor, and the point-cloud Close parameters. The SPACE itself (Round 24: THREE INTIMATE AXIS-ALIGNED ROOMS that age — Room 1 front/gay, Room 2 west/lesbian, Room 3 east/trans; doorways, per-era aging, Maya=Room 3, the lamp carry) lives in data/room/reinterp_deltas.json (generated by tools/gen_rooms.mjs) and folds via src/room/clusterMorph.ts. COLOR LAW: every hex here already exists in data/room/era1.json; e2-e4 rig hues re-derive when era2+ theme palettes land. zoneFill = the two side rooms' accent omnis (light-zoneE = Room 3, the trans room / light-zoneW = Room 2, the lesbian room), repositioned to the room centers ±3.88; mayaGlow = Maya's E4 interface light in Room 3.

witnessTerminal._note: the witness record plane's E1 position (4:3, same canvas), now the same footprint as the opening cork board so cork -> profile board -> witness record is one surface; from r2 on cluster.ts may ride only z during the cascade

ceilingWitness._note: R8-3: presence only — light/eye-motif, NEVER reading. A square iris (pixel discipline: 90° geometry) recessed in the ceiling over the room's center; a pale sourceless wash when awake. Dormant until the O7 first filing.

rigs._note: Per-era light targets for the era1.json light ids + scene ambient. The arc: E1 lamp-dominant night (~70/30 warm) → E2 office-grade fluorescent (~50/50, managed) → E3 platform pastel (near-shadowless diffuse, the lamp a leftover) → E4 interface-lit near-dark (the cold has won; the lamp survives as the one warm pocket, CARRIED to Maya's desk). 'hold' = T1's lamp-only breath (choreography §T1.1). 'close' kills the room for the point-cloud inversion. Session 66: `r2Lamp` is Vera's own desk lamp in Room 2 — the warm SOURCE the room lacked (it had only an invisible ceiling omni); it appears at E3 and is pulled down at E4 as the cold light wins, per the style direction's era arc.

e2._note: S2R.0a (Session 34): 2003 DAYLIGHT — the single strongest time-passage cue (E1 was lamp-lit night). `moonlight` (the window-direction light) recolors from era1.json's night-blue window hue to its own `moon` prop's warm hue (#F3EAD8, already approved in this file per the COLOR LAW above) and comes up from a near-off 0.05 to a real daytime presence — the ONE change from the prior office-fluorescent-only e2 rig; `lamp`/`roomFill`/`screenGlow`/`witnessCold` are unchanged (the lamp was already reduced from E1's 2.9, satisfying 'lamp glow reduced').

rigs._docE4RoomOneDark: ⛑ ROOM 1 GOES DARK PAST ITS OWN ERA (Sérgio, 2026-08-28: 'The room should go dark'). Under the frozen-in-time model each room keeps the era it was left in, which would have put Daniel's lit 1997 desk in 2026; his ruling is that you see the SHAPE of the room and not its objects. So Room 1's own two lights are off here: `roomFill` sits at [0,1.9,0.9] with range 5, which is Daniel's centre room, and `screenGlow` is the glow of a monitor that is switched off by E4 anyway (era3Devices: the last update draws on the workstation and Daniel's Era-3 monitor stays off) — it was lighting an empty room from a dead screen. ⛑ WHAT REPLACES IT, and why the numbers moved rather than just dropping: `roomFill` had been widened to range 8 and recoloured cold in E4, so it was doing double duty as the cluster-wide wash. Zeroing it alone would have taken Room 3 down with Room 1. The wash moves to the per-room accents instead — `zoneFill` 0.28 → 0.52 (light-zoneE/W at x=±3.88) and `mayaGlow` 1.35 → 1.55 — which light Rooms 2 and 3 from inside themselves and leave the centre unlit. ⛑ The travelling lamp is NOT touched: by E4 it has already moved to Maya's desk (cluster.ts: 'the lamp lives in Room 1 for E1-E3; at E4 its props move'), so it is Room 3's warmth here, not Room 1's.
rigs._docE4RoomTwoDark: ⛑ 2026-09-05 — AND ROOM 2 GOES DARK TOO, which is the same ruling one room over and four sessions late. Sérgio, on a screenshot of the E4 turn: *"the light is still on Vera, and it is supposed to be not."* `_docE4RoomOneDark` above records his 2026-08-28 decision that a room you have left shows its SHAPE and not its objects, and set Daniel's roomFill and screenGlow to 0 at e4 — and then nobody carried it to Vera, whose r2Lamp (0.55), r2Screen (0.4) and zoneW (0.52 via zoneFill) all stayed lit into 2026. ⚑ r2Screen was lighting a monitor that no longer exists there: the same day's fold removes w_flatPanelBody at r4. A glow with nothing to glow from. All three are 0 at e4 now. ⚑ `zoneW` is named here on purpose — see cluster.ts's zone loop, which used to overwrite every zone light with zoneFill AFTER the named pass, so r2Screen's authored 0.4 was never once the value it got.
rigs._docE4RoomsHeldNotDark: ⛑ 2026-09-05, SÉRGIO REVISING HIS OWN 2026-08-28 RULING, and he is right twice: *"To be totally honest we need some light source on the Vera and Daniel room, like a symbolic element of the existence, i fear that it looks like a scary movie being so dark, my bad."* Taking those rooms to 0 obeyed the letter of `_docE4RoomOneDark` and broke a LAW: CLAUDE.md's Soft Lo-Fi doctrine says rooms are cozy and "NOT horror-dark", with extremes forbidden. A room at zero is an extreme, and an emptied room at zero reads as a haunted house — which is a genre this work must never borrow, because the horror here is administrative and well-lit. ⚑ So each left room keeps ONE light on, low: roomFill 0.16 in Daniel's, r2Lamp 0.20 in Vera's, zoneW at 0.14 under it. Not a compromise between his two rulings — the SECOND one, executed. You still see the shape rather than the objects (Maya's room runs 0.95 lamp / 1.55 mayaGlow / 0.52 zoneE, three to five times brighter), and the meaning is better than darkness: a lamp left on is what a room has when someone left in a hurry, and this piece already says so — carryLampLight's own note is that nobody turned Daniel's off in thirty years. ⚑ r2Screen stays at 0: the monitor it glowed from was removed at r4 the same day, and a glow with no source is a lie, not an ember. ⚑ RAISED AGAIN 2026-09-05 (*"It should have more intensity the light, sorry"*): 0.16/0.20/0.14 → 0.34/0.46/0.28. My first pass at 'an ember' was still reading as a blackout with a candle in it. Maya's room still leads by roughly 2×, which is the ratio that matters — the left rooms should be quieter than hers, not invisible.

pointCloud._note: S92 — THE TWO VISUAL TIERS (REINTERP_THE_CLOSE_TREATMENT_2026-08-17.md §3, the piece's aesthetic law made literal: the witness side is the sharp side, surveillance is high-definition, life is soft). TWO populations, not one: APPARATUS nodes (data/strings/close_network.json's labels, one node per label, exactly) render COOL/#8899BB — already the piece's own witness-blue (witnessCold/moonlight), no new hue — sharp, full-opacity, LABELLED, and linked ONLY to each other in a guaranteed-connected chain (+ a few cross-links): traceable end to end, by construction. PERSON nodes (the dense core+satellite population, unchanged in count from the old single-tier build) render WARM (the lamp pool) at a capped, softer opacity, carry NO label and NO link to anything — not to the apparatus, not to each other. The system documents people; the piece refuses to: there is no line a player can follow from one soft node to another, and no line from a soft node to a labelled one. Backdrop stays night-blue (Round 18: never black).
pointCloud._docPersonSlotAspect: ⚑ A PERSON NODE IS A ROOM SEEN EDGE-ON, NOT A DOT. The piece has one grammar for `many rooms` — vertical lit slots in a dark field — used by the relocation choreography's building and the E4 finale's cyclorama (REINTERP_THE_BUILDING_2026-08-02.md). S92 built the Close's two tiers correctly and left every node a uniform cube, having verified that no SECOND visual language was invented without applying the FIRST; a cube field is a generic point cloud, and the whole point of the Close is that the player recognises this image from inside the piece. 3.6 is a window's proportion, not a tower's. ⚑ The APPARATUS tier stays square on purpose: it is an instrument, not a dwelling, and the shape difference does the same work as the colour and the labels — one tier is a place someone lives, the other is a thing that was built to sort them.
pointCloud._docTheOpening: ⚑ S101 — THE STARS ON THE CEILING BECOME THE NETWORK (Sérgio, 2026-09-02). The constellation no longer cuts in at full size: it starts as the small dense patch of glow-stars over the seat — `ceiling`, below, which is a real merged mesh sitting on the room's ceiling for the whole piece — and opens out around the player over `openSeconds`. Nothing is spawned and nothing is swapped: it is ONE root, lerped from the ceiling anchor at a small uniform scale to the sky's own centre at full size, so the stars a child put up are literally the nodes the network is made of. Uniform scale on purpose — the labels are quads on this root and a squashed axis would squash the text.

ceiling._doc: The glow-in-the-dark stars on the room's ceiling, over the seat — the object the Close's whole image is built on, and the reference Sérgio's own constellation brief names ("real glow-in-the-dark star stickers"). ONE merged mesh, one draw call, the person tier's own warm palette at a low level: they are a kid's, they are unlabelled, and nothing in the piece ever points at them. They fade out as the constellation opens from exactly their place.

pointCloud._docTheArcs: ⚑ S101 — ONE ARC PER ERA, AT ONE BEARING PER ERA. The apparatus nodes were a golden-angle spread, which is to say the network's shape said nothing at all; each anchor in data/strings/close_network.json now carries the era of the piece it grounds, and the geometry follows. Era 0 (the project's own frame) stays overhead where the ceiling was — the piece is looking at itself from underneath. Eras 1-4 hang at four bearings 90° apart, so reading the ending is the piece's one bodily gesture, the turn, spent one last time.

panel._doc: The four information panels, one per era, hanging over each era's own arc — one atlas, one mesh, one draw call. They face the centre and do NOT billboard: the panel is where it is, and you turn to read it. Sizes are metres at `radius` from the seat; a 1.62 m card at 2.95 m is about 31° of the frame, which is a page held at reading distance.
